intent.raw_query: Banff hiking and lakes, $2800 couple, 6 days, July 2027, from Calgary

experiences.name: Lake Louise Shoreline Hike
experiences.description: Walk the iconic turquoise shores of Lake Louise and continue up to the Plain of Six Glaciers teahouse for breathtaking views of Victoria Glacier. One of the most stunning alpine lake experiences in the Canadian Rockies.

experiences.name: Moraine Lake Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek
experiences.description: Hike the Rockpile Trail and Lakeshore Trail at the world-famous Moraine Lake, surrounded by ten soaring peaks. The vivid blue glacial water is unmatched in beauty and is best experienced before crowds arrive. Shuttle reservation required.

experiences.name: Johnston Canyon Icewalk
experiences.description: Follow a dramatic canyon trail past lower and upper waterfalls to the Ink Pots — vivid natural springs in an open meadow. Catwalk boardwalks cling to canyon walls for a thrilling and accessible nature experience suitable for all fitness levels.

experiences.name: Sulphur Mountain Gondola & Summit Boardwalk
experiences.description: Ride the gondola to 2,281 metres above sea level for panoramic views of six mountain ranges, then walk the 1 km summit boardwalk to the historic Sanson's Peak weather observatory. Alternatively, hike up the Sulphur Mountain Trail to save on cost.

experiences.name: Icefields Parkway Self-Drive & Peyto Lake Viewpoint
experiences.description: Drive one of the world's most scenic highways from Banff to Jasper, stopping at Peyto Lake — a wolf-head-shaped turquoise lake viewable from Bow Summit — along with Mistaya Canyon and the Weeping Wall. A full-day immersive nature experience through glacier-carved landscapes.
experiences.location: Icefields Parkway (Highway 93 North), Banff National Park

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Banff, Canada
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Lake Louise Shoreline Hike
experiences.description: Walk the iconic turquoise shores of Lake Louise and continue up to the Plain of Six Glaciers teahouse for breathtaking views of Victoria Glacier. One of the most stunning alpine lake experiences in the Canadian Rockies.

experiences.name: Johnston Canyon Icewalk
experiences.description: Follow a dramatic canyon trail past lower and upper waterfalls to the Ink Pots — vivid natural springs in an open meadow. Catwalk boardwalks cling to canyon walls for a thrilling and accessible nature experience suitable for all fitness levels.

day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary Airport at 14:00 on Flight AC. Collect luggage and take the Banff Airporter shuttle (~$60 CAD one-way) to Banff town. Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge and freshen up. Take a relaxed stroll along Banff Avenue to get oriented with the town.
day_by_day.evening: Walk down to the Bow River and enjoy the free Bow River Loop Trail for a gentle 1-hour sunset walk through pine forests and along the riverbank. A perfect low-key introduction to Banff's scenery.

meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or snack at the Calgary Airport before boarding the shuttle.
meals.dinner: Nourish Bistro on Banff Avenue — a budget-friendly vegetarian/vegan café with hearty bowls and wraps around $14–18 CAD. Great for a relaxed first evening.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Banff Airporter shuttle in advance online to secure your seat. Pick up a free Banff National Park trail map at the Banff Visitor Centre (224 Banff Ave) if it's still open on arrival. Note: A Parks Canada day pass (~$11 CAD/person) is required to enter the national park — consider purchasing a 6-day pass online for better value.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Icewalk — Start early (by 8:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Follow the dramatic canyon trail past the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km), then continue on to the magical Ink Pots — vivid natural mineral springs set in an open meadow. The full round trip is about 11 km and takes 3–4 hours. Trail is well-marked and mostly flat with boardwalks through the canyon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Johnston Canyon and have a picnic lunch at the trailhead or nearby Fireside Picnic Area. In the afternoon, head to the free Banff Gondola viewpoint area on Sulphur Mountain — skip the gondola ($65 CAD) and instead hike the Sulphur Mountain Trail (5.5 km one-way, ~2 hours up) for panoramic views of the Bow Valley at zero cost.
day_by_day.evening: Descend Sulphur Mountain and soak tired muscles at the nearby Banff Upper Hot Springs (~$16 CAD entry). Return to town for a budget dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab oatmeal, fruit, and coffee from a grocery store (Nesters Market on Marten St) the night before to self-cater a quick breakfast at the lodge.
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade picnic — sandwiches, trail mix, and fruit from Nesters Market. Eat at the Johnston Canyon picnic area.
meals.dinner: Tooloulou's on Caribou Street — casual Cajun-inspired comfort food with mains around $16–22 CAD. Try the jambalaya or a hearty burger.

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon gets very busy by mid-morning in July — arriving at 8:00 AM is strongly recommended. Wear sturdy shoes as the canyon boardwalks can be slippery. Bring a light rain jacket in case of afternoon showers (average 30 mm rain this month). The Sulphur Mountain hike saves you ~$65 CAD vs. the gondola and is a rewarding workout.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake — Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek. Depart by 6:00 AM as private vehicles are no longer permitted at Moraine Lake without a reservation. Take the Banff National Park shuttle from the Banff Gondola parking lot (book in advance at reservation.pc.gc.ca, ~$8 CAD round trip). Upon arrival, hike the Rockpile Trail (short 20-min loop) for the iconic panoramic view, then continue along the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km round trip) hugging the vivid turquoise shoreline surrounded by the ten soaring peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the lakeshore hike, take the shuttle back and stop at Lake Louise Village for lunch. In the afternoon, begin the Lake Louise Shoreline Hike — walk the famous turquoise shores of Lake Louise (2 km flat shoreline) before ascending to the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (~8.6 km round trip from the lake, moderate difficulty). Enjoy stunning glacier views along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff via the Roam Transit Bus 8X (Lake Louise Express, ~$10 CAD). Enjoy a quiet evening walk along Banff's town streets and browse local shops.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at the lodge — instant oatmeal, bananas, and coffee prepped the night before to allow a 6:00 AM departure.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from Nesters Market eaten at Moraine Lake or Lake Louise Village picnic tables. Keep it simple: wraps, cheese, apples, and trail mix.
meals.dinner: Banff Ave Brewing Co. — lively brewpub with pub-style mains (burgers, fish tacos) around $18–24 CAD. Happy hour deals available on select drinks.

day_by_day.notes: This is the most logistically demanding day — book the Moraine Lake shuttle and Lake Louise shuttle passes well in advance (they sell out fast in July). Bring sunscreen and layers as temperatures can drop near the glaciers even in summer. The Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse sells drinks and snacks — a hot tea there (~$5 CAD) is a lovely treat but optional for budget travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the iconic Tunnel Mountain Trail — a short but rewarding hike right from Banff townsite (2.3 km one-way, ~1.5 hours up). The summit offers sweeping 360° views of the Bow Valley, Banff town, and surrounding peaks. No shuttle needed — walk directly from the lodge. Start by 8:00 AM to enjoy quiet trails and cool morning temperatures.
day_by_day.afternoon: After descending, visit the free Banff Park Museum National Historic Site (on Banff Ave) — Canada's oldest natural history museum, free with your Parks Canada pass. Then rent a canoe at the Bow River Canoe Dock near the Fairmont Banff Springs (~$25 CAD/hour for a shared canoe) and paddle the scenic Bow River for an hour surrounded by mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the free Cave and Basin National Historic Site grounds at dusk (exterior boardwalk is free; interior exhibit ~$8 CAD) — the birthplace of Canada's national park system. Watch for wildlife near the wetlands at golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the lodge — eggs, toast, and fruit bought from Nesters Market.
meals.lunch: Grab a budget-friendly pita wrap or falafel from Aardvark Pizza & Sub on Banff Ave (~$12–15 CAD). Eat at Central Park along the Bow River.
meals.dinner: Masala Authentic Indian Cuisine — generous portions of curry, dal, and naan around $15–20 CAD. One of Banff's best-value sit-down restaurants.

day_by_day.notes: Tunnel Mountain is an excellent free activity perfectly suited for a mid-trip lighter day. Keep an eye out for elk grazing near the Tunnel Mountain campground area in the morning — they are commonly spotted here. The canoe rental is a fun and affordable way to experience the river without a guide.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a local bus along the Bow Valley Parkway (Highway 1A) — one of Canada's most scenic drives. Stop at the free Muleshoe Picnic Area and Backswamp Viewpoint for wildlife spotting (bears, elk, and deer are frequently seen). Continue to Johnston Canyon trailhead and take the short hike to the Lower Falls only if you want a quick revisit, or push on to Castle Mountain Viewpoint for dramatic free scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Vermilion Lakes — just 5 minutes from Banff townsite. Walk the free 5 km Vermilion Lakes Road (flat, easy, great for wildlife and photography). The three lakes reflect the surrounding mountains and are one of Banff's most beautiful and underrated spots. Bring binoculars if you have them — bald eagles and osprey are often spotted here.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff for a self-catered dinner at the lodge or a casual takeout meal. Spend the evening packing, reviewing photos, and relaxing. Optional: attend a free Parks Canada evening interpretive program at the Banff Visitor Centre (check schedule at the centre).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at the lodge before hitting the road.
meals.lunch: Picnic at Muleshoe Picnic Area along the Bow Valley Parkway — pack sandwiches and snacks from the grocery store.
meals.dinner: Laggan's Mountain Bakery & Deli at Lake Louise Village (if still in the area) for hearty sandwiches and baked goods under $15 CAD, OR pick up groceries from Nesters Market for a self-catered lodge dinner to save money on this penultimate night.

day_by_day.notes: The Bow Valley Parkway is free to drive and offers arguably better wildlife viewing than the Trans-Canada Highway. Speed limits are reduced to protect wildlife — drive slowly and watch for animals on the road. Vermilion Lakes is spectacular at sunset — time your visit for the golden hour if possible (around 9:00 PM in July).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise hike on the Fenland Trail, a peaceful 2 km loop through a boreal forest wetland just minutes from Banff townsite. It's flat, quiet, and ideal for a gentle last morning walk with excellent bird and beaver watching opportunities. Return to the lodge for a final breakfast and begin checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge and store luggage at the front desk. Spend your last free hours browsing the Banff Farmers Market (if running on Wednesdays/Thursdays — check local schedule) or pick up affordable souvenirs at the Banff Trading Post. Book the Banff Airporter return shuttle to Calgary Airport in advance — depart Banff with enough buffer time (journey ~1.5–2 hours) for your return flight.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to Calgary Airport. Enjoy a final meal at the airport or pack snacks for the journey home.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at the lodge using remaining groceries from Nesters Market — a great way to use up any leftover food and save money on the last day.
meals.lunch: Wild Flour Artisan Bakery & Café on Bear Street — excellent fresh-baked pastries, sandwiches, and coffee under $15 CAD. A perfect last Banff meal.
meals.dinner: Airport dining in Calgary or pack snacks for the flight to keep within budget.

day_by_day.notes: Book your return Banff Airporter shuttle at least 24–48 hours in advance to guarantee your seat. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight departure when leaving Banff, accounting for the 1.5–2 hour drive plus airport security. Return your Parks Canada pass if it was a day-use pass, or keep your annual pass if you plan to visit other Canadian parks this year. Total estimated budget for 6 days (excluding flights): $600–$850 CAD per person, including accommodation, shuttle transfers, park passes, meals (mix of self-catered and restaurants), and key activities.

trip_options.title: Classic Banff, Canada Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrival at 14:00. Travel from Calgary International Airport to Banff (~1.5 hours by shuttle or rental car).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge, freshen up, then take a leisurely stroll along the Bow River Trail in downtown Banff to get your bearings. Explore Banff Avenue, browse local shops, and visit the Banff Visitor Centre to pick up maps and park passes.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk up to Tunnel Mountain Trailhead viewpoint (easy 30-min hike from town) for sweeping panoramic views of the Bow Valley — a perfect low-key introduction to the Rockies.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack on the plane or at Calgary Airport before the drive.
meals.lunch: Pick up provisions at Nesters Market or grab a quick bite at Subway on Banff Avenue upon arrival.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bison Restaurant & Terrace — mid-range Canadian cuisine with locally sourced bison and seasonal ingredients. Mains ~CAD $28–40.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your Parks Canada Discovery Pass at the Banff Visitor Centre if you haven't already — it covers park entry for all 6 days and saves money. Confirm shuttle or car rental arrangements for the week. Banff Mountain Lodge is walking distance to most downtown amenities.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Sulphur Mountain Gondola & Summit Boardwalk. Ride the gondola to 2,281 metres for breathtaking 360° views of six mountain ranges. Walk the 1 km summit boardwalk to Sanson's Peak meteorological station. Allow 2–3 hours total. Book gondola tickets in advance online to avoid queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and head to Johnston Canyon Icewalk. Follow the dramatic canyon catwalk trail past the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km) to the vivid turquoise Ink Pots (5.8 km return). The canyon walls and waterfalls are stunning in summer light. Allow 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff town. Relax at the Banff Upper Hot Springs — a perfect muscle soak after a full day of activity (~CAD $20 entry). Then enjoy a quiet evening on Banff Avenue.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or grab pastries and coffee at Wild Flour Bakery Café — a Banff favourite with fresh-baked goods (~CAD $10–15).
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch from Nesters Market (sandwiches, fruit, trail mix) to enjoy at the Ink Pots meadow.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Elk + Oat — a popular mid-range gastropub with craft beers, burgers, and flatbreads. Mains ~CAD $20–32.

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon can get busy by mid-morning; aim to arrive by 9:00 AM for the afternoon slot or accept some crowds. Wear sturdy trail shoes as the canyon catwalk can be slippery near the waterfalls. Bring a light rain jacket just in case of afternoon showers.

day_by_day.morning: Very early departure (6:00–6:30 AM recommended) for Moraine Lake — the Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek. Private vehicles are restricted; take the Parks Canada shuttle from Banff or Lake Louise Lakeshore parking. Hike the Rockpile Trail for iconic views, then continue along the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km return) with the ten soaring peaks reflected in the impossibly blue water. Allow 3–4 hours of hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or shuttle the short distance to Lake Louise for the Lake Louise Shoreline Hike. Walk the turquoise shores of Lake Louise and continue up to the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (~13.8 km return, moderate). If energy allows, hike to the teahouse for a well-earned snack with glacier views. Alternatively, do the shorter lakeshore loop (4 km) if legs are tired from the morning.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and an early night — you've earned it after one of the most scenic days in the Canadian Rockies.

meals.breakfast: Grab a very early breakfast from the hotel or pre-pack granola bars and fruit the night before for the drive.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (cash only, ~CAD $15–20 per person) — a historic and uniquely scenic dining experience, or pack a lunch if you skip the teahouse hike.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tooloulou's Restaurant in Banff — Cajun-inspired comfort food at mid-range prices, a local favourite. Mains ~CAD $22–35.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake shuttle tickets must be booked weeks in advance on the Parks Canada reservation system — book these before your trip. Arrive at the shuttle depot early. Both Moraine Lake and Lake Louise are UNESCO World Heritage Sites; stay on marked trails and pack out all waste. This is the most demanding day of the itinerary — wear good hiking boots and bring sun protection.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Self-Drive — depart Banff by 8:00 AM heading north on Highway 93, one of the world's most scenic drives. First major stop: Bow Lake and Num-Ti-Jah Lodge viewpoint. Then continue to the Peyto Lake Viewpoint (Bow Summit, 2,069 m) — a wolf-shaped electric-blue lake framed by mountains and forest. Hike the short 0.8 km boardwalk trail to the upper viewpoint for the best perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north on the Icefields Parkway to the Columbia Icefield. Walk the Forefield Trail or take the Glacier Adventure onto Athabasca Glacier (optional add-on ~CAD $60–80). Visit the Glacier Skywalk for glass-floored views over the valley. Begin the drive back south, stopping at Sunwapta Falls and Athabasca Falls on the return.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Banff by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and stroll along the Bow River Pathway as the golden hour light hits the mountains.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel buffet or a quick stop at Café Aroma Internationale on Banff Avenue for coffee and a wrap.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch enjoyed at Peyto Lake viewpoint or Bow Lake — one of the most spectacular picnic spots on Earth. Pick up supplies the evening before from Nesters Market.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Coyotes Southwestern Grill — fresh, flavourful southwestern cuisine with vegetarian options. Mains ~CAD $20–30.

day_by_day.notes: Fill your gas tank in Banff before departing — fuel is limited and expensive along the Parkway. The full Banff–Jasper drive is 290 km one way; this itinerary turns around at the Columbia Icefield (~130 km from Banff) for a manageable day trip. Bring layers — temperatures at Bow Summit can be 5–8°C cooler than Banff town even in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Vermilion Lakes at sunrise — a short drive from town with stunning Rundle Mountain reflections and excellent wildlife viewing (beavers, herons, elk). Then hike the Fenland Trail (2 km loop, easy) through wetlands and old-growth forest near the Forty Mile Creek. A peaceful, unhurried morning in nature.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Lake Minnewanka — Banff's largest lake. Walk the Stewart Canyon Trail (7.6 km return, easy-moderate) along the lakeshore into a dramatic canyon carved by the Cascade River. Alternatively, book a Lake Minnewanka boat cruise (~CAD $55) for a scenic 1-hour tour with mountain and wildlife commentary.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Two Jack Lakeside for a golden-hour picnic or campfire (if fire permits allow) — one of the most photogenic spots near Banff with Mount Rundle reflected perfectly in the calm water. Return to town for a celebratory dinner on your second-to-last evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at the Whitebark Café — known for excellent eggs Benedict and locally roasted coffee (~CAD $15–20).
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Lake Minnewanka Snack Bar (seasonal, casual lakeside fare) or bring a picnic to enjoy at the lakeshore.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Park Distillery Restaurant + Bar — Banff's beloved mid-range restaurant serving Canadian campfire cuisine with house-distilled spirits. Mains ~CAD $25–38.

day_by_day.notes: Vermilion Lakes is best at dawn or dusk for wildlife and photography — set your alarm for 6:00 AM if possible. Lake Minnewanka boat cruises book up quickly in July; reserve online a day in advance. This is intentionally a lighter activity day to rest legs before the final day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning hike: Tunnel Mountain Summit Trail (4.8 km return, easy-moderate, ~1.5 hours) — a beloved Banff classic starting right from town. The 360° summit views over the Bow Valley, Banff townsite, and surrounding peaks make for a perfect farewell to the Rockies. Bring your camera for last memories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel, check out, and pack up. Spend your final hours browsing Banff Avenue for souvenirs — try Banff Trading Post or the Banff Candle Company. Visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies (free admission on some days, ~CAD $10 otherwise) for a cultural send-off and insight into the history of the Rockies.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Banff before departing for Calgary Airport (allow at least 2 hours for the drive plus check-in time). Depart Banff by 5:30–6:00 PM for most evening flights.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a treat at Eddie Burger + Bar for hearty Canadian breakfast poutine or eggs (~CAD $15–20).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Block Kitchen + Bar — modern Canadian fare with great sandwiches and salads, ideal for a relaxed final sit-down meal. ~CAD $18–28.
meals.dinner: Early farewell dinner at Saltlik Steakhouse — a Banff institution for celebrating a special occasion with Alberta beef. Mains ~CAD $35–55; splurge-worthy for the final night.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at Banff Mountain Lodge is typically 11:00 AM — ask about a late check-out if your flight departs late evening. Leave extra time for the Calgary Airport drive in case of wildlife on the Trans-Canada Highway (elk and bears are common). Reflect on an incredible week in one of the world's most beautiful national parks!

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 14:00. Travel time from Calgary International Airport to Banff Mountain Lodge is approximately 1.5 hours by private transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Banff Mountain Lodge and check in. After freshening up, take a leisurely private guided orientation walk through downtown Banff, strolling along Banff Avenue, visiting the Cascade Gardens, and soaking in your first views of Cascade Mountain. Stop at the Banff Park Museum and enjoy the crisp mountain air as you settle into the alpine atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace or rooftop lounge with panoramic mountain views. Enjoy a welcome dinner at The Maple Leaf Restaurant — one of Banff's finest dining establishments — featuring Canadian wild game, Alberta beef, and locally foraged ingredients paired with an exceptional wine list.

meals.lunch: Light charcuterie and welcome amenities arranged by the lodge upon arrival
meals.dinner: The Maple Leaf Restaurant — try the Alberta bison tenderloin or wild Pacific salmon with a curated Canadian wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private luxury transfer from Calgary Airport in advance (Mercedes Sprinter or similar). Confirm lodge check-in time and request early luggage drop if needed. Hydrate well on arrival — Banff sits at 1,383 m elevation and mild altitude adjustment is common.

day_by_day.morning: Sulphur Mountain Gondola & Summit Boardwalk: Begin the day with a ride on the Banff Gondola to 2,281 metres above sea level. Walk the 1 km Summit Boardwalk along the ridge, taking in sweeping panoramic views of six mountain ranges, the Bow Valley, and the town of Banff below. Visit the rooftop observation deck and the Sanson's Peak weather station. Ideal in the morning before afternoon crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the base of Sulphur Mountain and visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs — Canada's highest hot springs — for a restorative soak in mineral-rich thermal waters at 37–40°C with dramatic mountain backdrops. Follow with a premium spa treatment at the Willow Stream Spa (if staying at Fairmont Banff Springs nearby) or the lodge's own spa facilities for a deep tissue or hot stone massage.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at Eden Restaurant at the Rimrock Resort Hotel, Banff's most celebrated fine dining destination. Enjoy an intimate, award-winning tasting menu with impeccable views of the Bow Valley. Sommelier-guided wine pairings are highly recommended.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet in-room or lodge dining breakfast — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh fruit, and pressed juices
meals.lunch: Sky Bistro at the top of the Banff Gondola — elevated Canadian cuisine with floor-to-ceiling mountain views
meals.dinner: Eden Restaurant at Rimrock Resort — multi-course tasting menu featuring French-Canadian fusion and rare cellar wine selections

day_by_day.notes: Book Banff Gondola tickets and Sky Bistro lunch reservations in advance, especially for peak July season. Hot Springs are open daily; private spa bookings should be made 48 hours ahead. Wear layers — the summit can be 5–10°C cooler than town even in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Shoreline Hike: Depart early by private vehicle to Lake Louise (approximately 45 minutes from Banff). Walk the iconic turquoise shoreline of Lake Louise and continue up the well-maintained trail to the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse — a legendary alpine hut at 2,135 m offering homemade soups, baked goods, and unparalleled views of Victoria Glacier. The round-trip hike is approximately 13.8 km with 365 m elevation gain — moderate difficulty, highly rewarding.
day_by_day.afternoon: After descending, visit the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise for a refined lakeside lunch on their terrace. Spend the early afternoon exploring the Lake Louise shoreline at a relaxed pace, renting a canoe for a private paddle on the impossibly turquoise glacial waters — one of the most iconic experiences in the Canadian Rockies.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff for a relaxed evening. Pre-dinner drinks at the Bear Street Tavern or the Banff Ave Brewing Co. rooftop patio. Dinner at Juniper Bistro — a hidden gem with stunning valley views, creative Canadian menus, and a warm, intimate atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before departure — packed gourmet trail snacks and thermos coffee provided for the hike
meals.lunch: Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise — Lakeview Lounge or Walliser Stube for fondue and Swiss-Canadian alpine cuisine
meals.dinner: Juniper Bistro — seasonal Canadian menu with locally sourced proteins and a curated craft cocktail list

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 7:30 AM to secure parking or arrange a private driver. Lake Louise can be extremely crowded by 9 AM in July. Wear proper hiking boots and bring trekking poles for the Plain of Six Glaciers ascent. The teahouse is cash-only — bring Canadian currency. Canoe rentals at the lake are first-come, first-served; arrive early or book through the Chateau concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake — Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek: Take the mandatory Parks Canada shuttle or private reservation vehicle to Moraine Lake (private vehicles are no longer permitted without a reservation). Hike the Rockpile Trail for the world-famous viewpoint over the Valley of the Ten Peaks — the image that once graced the Canadian $20 bill. Continue along the Lakeshore Trail for a full immersive experience of the vivid blue-green lake framed by ten soaring peaks. The combined trails cover approximately 3–4 km with minimal elevation — accessible yet breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the lodge at the lakeside (arranged in advance). Spend the afternoon at leisure at Moraine Lake — consider a private guided canoe excursion on the lake for an up-close perspective of the glacial waters and surrounding peaks. Return to Banff by private transfer in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a private in-room dining experience at Banff Mountain Lodge — a curated multi-course dinner delivered to your suite with a bottle of premium Canadian or Old World wine. Alternatively, visit Saltlik Steakhouse for prime Alberta beef in a sophisticated setting.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast — avocado toast, Alberta eggs, smoked meats, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Luxury gourmet picnic box prepared by the lodge — artisan cheeses, charcuterie, smoked salmon, fresh bread, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Saltlik Steakhouse — prime dry-aged Alberta ribeye or tenderloin with truffle sides and a premium Napa Valley Cabernet

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake access requires advance shuttle booking through Parks Canada Reservation System or a private licensed operator — book weeks in advance for July. Arrive at the shuttle departure point by 6:30 AM for the best light and smallest crowds. The lake's colour is most vivid mid-morning. Weather can shift quickly; bring a light rain shell.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Self-Drive & Peyto Lake Viewpoint: Embark on one of the world's most celebrated scenic drives — the Icefields Parkway (Highway 93) heading north from Banff toward Jasper. Stop at Bow Lake, a serene glacial lake with views of Bow Glacier, then ascend to the Peyto Lake Viewpoint — a wolf-head-shaped turquoise lake set amid dense boreal forest and rocky peaks, considered one of the most photographed views in Canada. Continue north to Mistaya Canyon for a short trail walk through a stunning limestone gorge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Johnston Canyon Icewalk: On the return south, stop at Johnston Canyon — a dramatic canyon trail featuring a series of catwalks bolted into the canyon walls. Walk past the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km) to the vivid Ink Pots — seven natural cold mineral springs that bubble up in brilliant shades of blue, green, and turquoise set in an open meadow. The full round trip is approximately 11 km. Return to Banff by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the penultimate evening with cocktails at the Banff Springs Hotel's Rundle Bar — a storied, grand historic bar inside the iconic castle hotel. Follow with dinner at 1888 Chop House inside the Fairmont Banff Springs — a legendary steakhouse serving prime cuts in a magnificent historic dining room.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast — packed to-go snacks and premium thermos coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Num-Ti-Jah Lodge at Bow Lake — a rustic, historic lakeside lodge serving hearty Canadian lunches in a stunning setting
meals.dinner: 1888 Chop House, Fairmont Banff Springs — prime Alberta beef, wild game, and an iconic cellar wine list in a grand castle setting

day_by_day.notes: Rent a premium vehicle (Range Rover, Audi Q7, or similar) for the self-drive, or hire a private guide-driver who can narrate the ecology and geology of the Parkway. Fill the fuel tank before departing Banff — gas stations are scarce along the Parkway. Total driving distance for the day is approximately 250–280 km round trip; allow 10–12 hours. Start by 7:00 AM for the best light at Peyto Lake.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — sleep in and enjoy a luxurious late breakfast at the lodge. Take a slow, reflective walk along the Bow River Trail directly from the lodge — a flat, scenic 2–3 km stroll through pine forest along the Bow River with views of Mount Rundle and the Fairholme Range. Stop at Surprise Corner Viewpoint for a classic postcard view of the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel framed by Sulphur Mountain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the final afternoon exploring Banff Avenue's premium boutiques — pick up Canadian art, Indigenous artisan crafts, or luxury outdoor gear as souvenirs. Visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies for a curated cultural experience. Enjoy a farewell spa treatment or float session at the lodge to rest the legs after a week of hiking.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Towa — a modern Japanese-Canadian fusion restaurant in Banff offering an elegant omakase-style experience with wagyu, fresh seafood, and creative seasonal menus. Toast to an extraordinary week in the Canadian Rockies.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent lodge breakfast — eggs royale, smoked salmon, fresh fruit platters, house-made granola, and mimosas
meals.lunch: Crave Mountain Grill or Block Kitchen & Bar — casual yet refined lunch with craft cocktails or local craft beer
meals.dinner: Towa Restaurant — omakase or à la carte Japanese-Canadian fusion with premium sake or cocktail pairing

day_by_day.notes: If departing the following morning, arrange a private luxury transfer back to Calgary Airport (allow 2 hours travel time plus check-in buffer). Pack hiking gear carefully — muddy boots should be stored in provided bags. Confirm any outstanding spa or dining charges with the lodge before checkout. Consider a Parks Canada annual discovery pass as a meaningful keepsake of the trip.
